chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ فَارِسٍ، عَنِ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنِ الشَّهَابِ بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ، عَنِ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Masud, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Faris, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Shihab ibn Abd Rabbi, from Abi Basir who said:

chunks.arabic_text: إِنَّ عُلْبَاءَ الْأَسَدِيَّ وَلِيَ الْبَحْرَيْنَ فَأَفَادَ سَبْعِينَ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَدَوَابَّ وَرِقَاقًا، قَالَ: فَحَمَلَ ذَلِكَ كُلَّهُ حَتَّى وَضَعَهُ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ ثُمَّ قَالَ: إِنِّي وَلِيتُ الْبَحْرَيْنَ لِبَنِي أُمَيَّةَ وَأَفَدْتُ كَذَا وَكَذَا وَقَدْ حَمَلْتُهُ كُلَّهُ إِلَيْكَ وَعَلِمْتُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لَمْ يَجْعَلْ لَهُمْ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئًا وَأَنَّهُ كُلُّهُ لَكَ، فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: هَاتِهِ، فَوَضَعَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ: قَدْ قَبِلْنَا مِنْكَ وَوَهَبْنَاهُ لَكَ وَأَحْلَلْنَاكَ مِنْهُ وَضَمِنَّا لَكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْجَنَّةَ

translations.en: Indeed, 'Ulba al-Asadi assumed the governorship of Bahrayn and gained seventy thousand gold coins, livestock and slaves. He said: He carried all that with him until he placed it in front of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: I was appointed the governor of Bahrayn by Bani Umayya and have gained such and such, and I have brought it all to you, and I know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not give them anything of it, and that it all belongs to you. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: Hand it over. So he placed it in front of him. He said to him: We have accepted from you, and we have gifted it back to you, and we have permitted you to make use of it, and we have guaranteed for you Paradise on behalf of Allah.

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبِي بَصِيرٌ: فَقُلْتُ مَا بِي، فَبَكَيْتُ، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ: جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ أَلَسْتُ الْكَبِيرَ السِّنِّ الضَّرِيرَ الْبَصَرِ فَاضْمُنْهَا لِي، قَالَ: قَدْ فَعَلْتُ، قُلْتُ: أَضْمِنْهَا لِي عَلَى آبَائِكَ وَسَمِّهِمْ وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا، قَالَ: قَدْ فَعَلْتُ، قُلْتُ: فَاضْمُنْهَا لِي عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَ: قَدْ فَعَلْتُ، قُلْتُ: أَضْمِنْهَا لِي عَلَى اللَّهِ، قَالَ: قَدْ فَعَلْتُ

translations.en: Abi Basir said: So I said: What is wrong with me? and I began crying, then I said: May I be your ransom, am I not the old in age, weak in sight? So guarantee it for me. He said: I have done so. I said: Guarantee it to me on behalf of your forefathers and name them one by one. He said: I have done so. I said: Guarantee it for me on behalf of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: I have done so. I said: Guarantee it for me on behalf of Allah. He said: I have done so.

en.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kashi* highlights the concept of *al-ghanimat* (booty/wealth) belonging to the Imam, illustrating how 'Ulba al-Asadi returned the Umayyad governor's surplus to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) as a divine right. The Imam’s acceptance and subsequent guarantee of Paradise for 'Ulba, followed by Abi Basir’s playful yet profound request for intercession through the lineage of the Prophet and the Imams, underscores the Shia belief in the spiritual authority and intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt. This narrative serves as a practical example of *tawassul* (seeking means of approach) and the transfer of worldly wealth to the Imam for spiritual benefit.
en.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imam guaranteeing Paradise to 'Ulba al-Asadi and Abi Basir?

key_terms.آباؤك: Your forefathers (referring to the Imams' lineage)
